title: Combining the three components
prompt: A 29-year-old cyclist is assessed after a collision before receiving sedatives. He opens his eyes when addressed, speaks coherently but is disoriented, and obeys a two-part command. No injury prevents assessment. Which Glasgow Coma Scale score correctly records these findings?
explanation: Eye opening to sound scores 3, confused speech 4, and obeying commands 6.

distractorExplanations.E3 V4 M6 = 13: Eye opening to sound scores 3, confused speech 4, and obeying commands 6.
distractorExplanations.E4 V4 M6 = 14: The eyes do not open spontaneously, so E4 is incorrect.
distractorExplanations.E3 V5 M6 = 14: Coherent but disoriented speech is not fully oriented V5.
distractorExplanations.E3 V4 M5 = 12: Following commands is M6, not localizing M5.
distractorExplanations.E2 V3 M6 = 11: The patient opens to sound and converses, rather than opening only to pressure and using isolated words.

title: An intubated patient
prompt: A 54-year-old patient is reassessed after intubation. Sedation has been paused, and he opens his eyes spontaneously and follows commands. The endotracheal tube prevents speech. Under the structured Glasgow Coma Scale approach, which record best represents the examination?
answer: E4 VNT M6, with the reason documented and no total calculated
options: E4 VNT M6, with the reason documented and no total calculated
explanation: The tube makes the verbal component non-testable; assigning a number would misrepresent the finding.

distractorExplanations.E4 VNT M6, with the reason documented an: The tube makes the verbal component non-testable; assigning a number would misrepresent the finding.
distractorExplanations.E4 V1 M6 = 11: V1 would imply an assessable absence of verbal response.
distractorExplanations.E4 V5 M6 = 15: Orientation cannot be assumed from command following alone.
distractorExplanations.E4 V0 M6 = 10: Zero is not a valid verbal score.
distractorExplanations.E4 V4 M6 = 14: There is no observed confused verbal response to justify V4.

title: Localizing versus withdrawal
prompt: An adult with impaired consciousness does not follow commands. During an appropriate head-and-neck pressure stimulus, he purposefully brings his hand above the clavicle toward the stimulus. There is no paralysis or limb injury. Which best motor score describes this response?
explanation: A purposeful movement toward the head-and-neck stimulus is localizing.

distractorExplanations.M5: localizing: A purposeful movement toward the head-and-neck stimulus is localizing.
distractorExplanations.M4: normal flexion: Simple flexion away from a stimulus is different from purposeful localization.
distractorExplanations.M3: abnormal flexion: This requires a predominantly abnormal flexion pattern.
distractorExplanations.M2: extension: Extension is not the movement described.

title: A mechanically untestable eye response
prompt: A 40-year-old man has severe bilateral eyelid swelling after facial trauma. His eyelids cannot open mechanically, although he is conversing and following commands. Which eye-component entry avoids confusing a local injury with impaired consciousness during Glasgow Coma Scale assessment?
options: E1 because no opening is seen
explanation: Mechanical obstruction makes eye opening non-testable.

distractorExplanations.ENT, documenting the local obstruction: Mechanical obstruction makes eye opening non-testable.
distractorExplanations.E1 because no opening is seen: E1 requires no response without a local factor preventing assessment.
distractorExplanations.E2 because trauma is painful: Pain alone does not establish an observed eye-opening response.
distractorExplanations.E3 because the patient speaks: Speech cannot substitute for observed eye opening.
distractorExplanations.E4 because commands are followed: Motor performance does not establish spontaneous eye opening.

title: A neurological change over time
prompt: At 09:00 an unsedated patient is E4 V5 M6. At 09:30 he opens his eyes only when addressed, uses isolated intelligible words without conversation, and still obeys commands. No new local limitation is present. Which record correctly documents the later examination?
explanation: Sound-evoked opening and isolated words score E3 and V3; command following remains M6.

distractorExplanations.E3 V3 M6 = 12: Sound-evoked opening and isolated words score E3 and V3; command following remains M6.
distractorExplanations.E3 V4 M6 = 13: V4 requires coherent communication despite disorientation.
distractorExplanations.E2 V3 M6 = 11: The eyes open to sound, not only to pressure.
distractorExplanations.E4 V3 M6 = 13: The eye response is no longer spontaneous.
distractorExplanations.E3 V2 M5 = 10: Intelligible words are V3, and obeying commands is M6.
